userStories.title: Memory config
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the defaulted repository-wide memory configuration and typed accessor.

**Motivation** — Feature 1 shipped the storage but nothing in nax reads or writes it yet.

**Approach** — Config (`memory`)
```jsonc
"memory": {
  "enabled": true,          // false: no host, no tools, no section, no sync
  "provider": "local",      // only "local" is accepted in this feature
  "writeMode": "direct",    // "direct" | "proposal"
  "indexBytes": 24576,      // integer, 512..262144; the injected index's byte cap
  "askOnSave": true         // guarded native chat asks before nax-memory__save / __forget
}
```
`MemoryConfigSchema` is a `.strict()` zod object (like `schemas-mcp.ts`): an unknown key such as `stages` or `koda` fails validation until the feature that owns it widens the schema. `provider` is `z.enum(["local"])`. It is wired into `NaxConfigSchema` as `memory: MemoryConfigSchema.default(() => MemoryConfigSchema.parse({}))`; `src/config/schemas.ts` is at 591 of 600 lines and gains about three.

`NaxConfig` is a hand-written interface (`src/config/runtime-types.ts:513`, 599 of 600 lines). Following the `mcp` precedent (`mcp?: import("./runtime-types-mcp").McpConfig`), the type lives in `src/config/runtime-types-memory.ts` (`MemoryConfig { enabled: boolean; provider: "local"; writeMode: "direct" | "proposal"; indexBytes: number; askOnSave: boolean }`) and `NaxConfig` gains one line, `memory?: import("./runtime-types-memory").MemoryConfig;`, bringing the file to exactly 600. `MemoryConfig` is re-exported from `src/config/types.ts` and `src/config/index.ts`. Because the field is optional on the type, every reader goes through `memoryConfigOf(config: Pick<NaxConfig, "memory">): MemoryConfig` (in `schemas-memory.ts`, exported from `@/config`), which returns `config.memory` or the schema default. The rest of this spec writes `memoryConfigOf(config).x`.

`memory` is a repository-wide setting read from the resolved config (global then project); per-package `.nax/mono/<pkg>/config.json` files do not change it. `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` (`src/cli/config-descriptions.ts`) gains `memory`, `memory.enabled`, `memory.provider`, `memory.writeMode`, `memory.indexBytes`, `memory.askOnSave`.

**Scope** — In: the two new config modules, schema/interface wiring, config barrels, descriptions and adding memory to the defaults test's closed key list. Out: paths/host/tool consumers (US-002 onward), chat askRules (US-014). Feature boundaries: The koda remote provider, the `memory.koda` config block, `nax memory link` and provider-side search merging are the `memory-koda-provider` feature; `memory.provider` accepts only `local` here. `memory` is not read from per-package `.nax/mono/<pkg>/config.json` files. Run-stage delivery (`memory.stages`, the memory context element, run-host sync, the reporter line) and bot review / fix surfaces are the `memory-run-stages` feature; `nax run` gets no memory tools or index from this feature.

**Interface** — `MemoryConfigSchema`, `memoryConfigOf(config: Pick<NaxConfig, "memory">): MemoryConfig`, `MemoryConfig { enabled: boolean; provider: "local"; writeMode: "direct" | "proposal"; indexBytes: number; askOnSave: boolean }`. Verify source files remain <=600 lines without adding gate assertions to ACs.

userStories.title: Memory directories
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve collision-resistant per-project and shared user mirror directories.

**Motivation** — Feature 1 shipped the storage but nothing in nax reads or writes it yet.

**Approach** — Directories (`paths.ts`)
`hash8` is the first 8 lowercase hex characters of the SHA-256 of `realpath(repoRoot)` (UTF-8), so two repositories with the same basename get different mirrors and a symlinked checkout shares the real one's mirror. The project key is `getProjectKey(config, repoRoot)` (`src/config/project-key.ts`) passed through `memoryProjectSegment`. Here use the resolved canonical repository root for identity, including getProjectKey's basename fallback: a symlink with a different basename must still produce the same whole projectDir, not merely the same hash suffix, as required by the symlink-equality AC. Preserve the original caller repoRoot in error context. `globalConfigDir()` (`src/config/paths/index.ts`) is the only way to reach `~/.nax` (the `check:no-real-global-nax` gate). A `realpath` failure throws `NaxError` code `MEMORY_REPO_ROOT_UNRESOLVED` with context `{ stage: "memory", repoRoot, cause }`.

`MemoryLogger` (declared in `paths.ts`, re-exported by the barrel) is `Pick<Logger, "warn" | "debug" | "info" | "error">` from `@/logger`; it is structurally assignable to nax-agent's `AgentLogger`, which feature 1's functions take, and the plain-object fallback logger in `src/cli/chat.ts` satisfies it.

**Scope** — In: paths.ts, _memoryPathsDeps, and creation of src/memory/index.ts; every later story that adds a src/memory export appends it there. Out: repo-note reading (US-003/004), host composition (US-005).

**Interface**
```ts
export type MemoryLogger = Pick<Logger, "warn" | "debug" | "info" | "error">;
export interface MemoryDirs {
  readonly root: string;       // <globalConfigDir()>/memory
  readonly projectDir: string; // <root>/projects/<segment>-<hash8>
  readonly userDir: string;    // <root>/user
}
export function memoryProjectSegment(projectKey: string): string; // [A-Za-z0-9._-] kept, every other char -> "-"
export async function memoryDirs(input: { readonly config: Pick<NaxConfig, "name">; readonly repoRoot: string }): Promise<MemoryDirs>;
export const _memoryPathsDeps: { realpath: (path: string) => Promise<string> };
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With the global config directory pointed at a temp dir, memoryDirs({ config: { name: "api" }, repoRoot }) returns projectDir <globalDir>/memory/projects/api-<h> where <h> is the first 8 lowercase hex characters of the SHA-256 of realpath(repoRoot).
[unit] memoryDirs returns userDir equal to <globalDir>/memory/user.
[unit] memoryDirs returns root equal to <globalDir>/memory.
[unit] Two temp repositories both named api in different parents get different projectDir values from memoryDirs with config: {}.
[unit] memoryDirs called with a symlink to a repository returns the same projectDir as with the repository's real path.
[unit] memoryDirs with config: {} uses the repository directory's basename as the project key segment.
[unit] memoryProjectSegment("team/api v2") returns team-api-v2.
[unit] memoryProjectSegment("nax-monorepo.v1_x") returns nax-monorepo.v1_x.
[unit] When _memoryPathsDeps.realpath rejects, memoryDirs throws NaxError with code MEMORY_REPO_ROOT_UNRESOLVED.
[unit] That NaxError's context.cause is the rejection.
[unit] That NaxError's context.stage is memory.
[unit] Importing memoryDirs and memoryProjectSegment from @/memory succeeds.

routing.reasoning: Small path abstraction, but SHA-256 identity and realpath/symlink confinement merit the security override and strict isolated tests.

userStories.title: Repo notes: per-file rules
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read validated top-level team notes without following candidate links or exposing secrets.

**Motivation** — This feature is the first surface: the agent sees an index of what earlier sessions saved, reads notes on demand, saves what a future session would need, and the user can inspect and edit memory from the terminal.

**Approach** — Repo-committed team notes (`repo-notes.ts`), rules 2 and 3:
A repo note is a feature-1 note file, so it has every frontmatter key `parseMemoryNote` requires and one blank line between the closing `---` and the body. Example `.nax/memory/staging-db.md`:
```markdown
---
id: staging-db
slug: staging-db
type: project
scope: project
description: the staging database is shared; never reset it
source: human
updatedAt: 2026-11-02T08:00:00Z
status: active
---

Ask in #infra before running migrations against staging.
```
2. Only top-level names ending `.md` are candidates; subdirectories and other names are ignored (not counted as skipped). Candidates are taken in file-name order.
3. A candidate is skipped when: it is not a regular file by `lstat` (a symlink is never followed); it is larger than `REPO_NOTE_MAX_FILE_BYTES` (checked from `lstat` before reading); reading it fails; `parseMemoryNote` throws; its `slug` differs from the file name without `.md`; its `scope` is not `project`; its `status` is not `active`; or `findSecret` finds a secret in the description or the body. Each skip logs one `warn("memory", "repo note skipped", { path, reason })`; for a secret `reason` is `secret (<kind>)` and never contains the matched text.
Accepted notes are returned with `source` replaced by `"repo"`. Repo notes are never written by any tool or command.

**Scope** — In: repo-notes.ts per-file validation, deterministic order, skip accounting and exports from the memory barrel. Out: parent-directory safety and accepted-note cap (US-004); host warning deduplication and merging (US-005).

**Interface**
```ts
export const REPO_NOTE_MAX_FILE_BYTES = 16_384;
export const REPO_NOTES_MAX = 200;
export interface RepoNotes {
  readonly notes: readonly MemoryNote[];   // accepted, source "repo", sorted by slug
  readonly skipped: number;                // candidates rejected by a rule below
}
export async function readRepoNotes(input: { readonly repoRoot: string; readonly logger: MemoryLogger }): Promise<RepoNotes>;
export const _repoNotesDeps: { lstat; readdir; readFile };   // node:fs/promises signatures
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] readRepoNotes({ repoRoot, logger }) on a repository holding the Design's example .nax/memory/staging-db.md returns notes with one note whose slug is staging-db.
[unit] That returned note's source is repo.
[unit] A file .nax/memory/other.md whose frontmatter slug is staging-db is not returned.
[unit] Skipping other.md logs one warn repo note skipped whose data path ends with other.md.
[unit] A file .nax/memory/bad.md with no frontmatter is not returned.
[unit] With only bad.md present, skipped is 1.
[unit] A note whose frontmatter scope is user is not returned.
[unit] A note whose frontmatter status is pending is not returned.
[unit] A symlink .nax/memory/link.md pointing at a valid note file is not returned.
[unit] A file larger than REPO_NOTE_MAX_FILE_BYTES (16384) is not returned.
[unit] For that oversized file, _repoNotesDeps.readFile is not called.
[unit] When _repoNotesDeps.readFile rejects for a candidate, that candidate is not returned and is counted in skipped.
[unit] A note whose body contains AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP is not returned.
[unit] The warn for that note has reason equal to secret (aws).
[unit] A notes.txt file and a valid note inside .nax/memory/sub/ produce no returned note.
[unit] With only those two present, skipped is 0.
[unit] Three valid notes with slugs zeta, alpha, mid are returned in the order alpha, mid, zeta.
[unit] Importing readRepoNotes from @/memory succeeds.

routing.reasoning: New bounded reader uses established codec, but secret detection and symlink read restrictions are security-critical.

suggestedCriteria: A repo note whose description contains AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP is skipped with reason secret (aws).
A secret skip warning contains no matched secret text.

userStories.title: Repo notes: directory safety and limit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Harden repository note directory traversal and bound the accepted-note scan.

**Motivation** — Feature 1 shipped the storage but nothing in nax reads or writes it yet.

**Approach** — Repo-committed team notes, rules 1 and 4, applied around US-003's rules in the specified order:
1. If `<repoRoot>/.nax` or `<repoRoot>/.nax/memory` is a symlink (`lstat`), no note is read, one warn `"repo notes directory is a symlink"` with `{ path }` is logged and the result is `{ notes: [], skipped: 0 }`. A missing directory returns `{ notes: [], skipped: 0 }` with no log. A `readdir` error other than a missing directory logs one warn `"repo notes unreadable"` with `{ path, error }` and returns `{ notes: [], skipped: 0 }`.
4. After `REPO_NOTES_MAX` accepted notes the remaining candidates are not read; one warn `"repo notes over limit"` with `{ skipped }` (their count) is logged and they count as skipped.

**Scope** — In: extending readRepoNotes with pre-listing parent lstat checks, missing/unreadable handling, cap and aggregate warning. Out: host composition and warning deduplication (US-005); do not rewrite the per-file codec/validation completed in US-003.

**Interface** — `export async function readRepoNotes(input: { readonly repoRoot: string; readonly logger: MemoryLogger }): Promise<RepoNotes>;` and `export const REPO_NOTES_MAX = 200;` remain the US-003 contract; use `_repoNotesDeps: { lstat; readdir; readFile }` with node:fs/promises signatures.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] readRepoNotes on a repository with no .nax/memory directory returns { notes: [], skipped: 0 }.
[unit] That call logs nothing.
[unit] When .nax/memory is a symlink to a directory holding a valid note, readRepoNotes returns no note.
[unit] That call logs one warn repo notes directory is a symlink.
[unit] When .nax itself is a symlink to a directory holding memory/staging-db.md, readRepoNotes returns no note.
[unit] When _repoNotesDeps.readdir rejects with an EACCES error, readRepoNotes returns { notes: [], skipped: 0 }.
[unit] That call logs one warn repo notes unreadable.
[unit] With REPO_NOTES_MAX + 2 valid notes present, readRepoNotes returns REPO_NOTES_MAX notes.
[unit] That call returns skipped equal to 2.
[unit] That call logs one warn repo notes over limit with skipped 2.

routing.reasoning: Parent symlink restrictions are a security boundary; the bounded scanner otherwise extends the existing reader.

suggestedCriteria: After 200 notes have been accepted, readRepoNotes does not read any remaining candidate file.
When .nax itself is a symlink, readRepoNotes logs one repo notes directory is a symlink warning naming that path.

userStories.title: Memory host: index, sync and status
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete the host's index rendering, synchronization and inspectable status.

**Motivation** — This feature is the first surface: the agent sees an index of what earlier sessions saved, reads notes on demand, saves what a future session would need, and the user can inspect and edit memory from the terminal.

**Approach** — Replace the three US-005 placeholders with the specified compositions:
- `renderIndex` = `renderMemoryIndex({ projectNotes: await notes("project"), userNotes: await notes("user"), decisions: await store.readDecisions(), heldForgets: await outbox.heldKeys("forget"), maxBytes: memoryConfigOf(config).indexBytes })`.
- `sync` = `syncMemory({ store, outbox, provider, logger })` (never throws by feature 1's contract).
- `status`: `notes.project` and `notes.user` count the mirror's notes of that scope as `store.listNotes` returns them; `notes.repo` counts repo notes that are not shadowed; `lastPullAt` / `lastError` come from `store.readSyncState()`; `queued` / `rejected` from `outbox.list()`.
Repo notes are read on each call of `notes`, `getNote`, `search`, `renderIndex` and `status` (no cache).
With the `local` provider, `pull` returns nothing and `reachable` is always true, so the syncs this feature wires (open, compaction, close) only drain the outbox; they still take the mirror lock and may return `locked` while another chat holds it. They are wired now so feature 3's remote provider needs no new call sites.

**Scope** — In: renderIndex, sync and status in host.ts using the existing _memoryHostDeps seam and MemoryStatus interface. Out: write methods (US-007), lifecycle sync call sites (US-013/014) and remote provider logic.

**Interface** — `renderIndex(): Promise<RenderedMemoryIndex>; sync(): Promise<MemorySyncResult>; status(): Promise<MemoryStatus>;` on `MemoryHost`. `MemorySyncResult.outcome: "synced" | "unreachable" | "locked" | "failed"`; renderer returns `{ text, omitted }`. `MemoryStatus` includes enabled:true, provider, writeMode, projectDir, userDir, lastPullAt, lastError, queued, rejected, notes:{project,user,repo}, repoSkipped as declared by US-005.

userStories.title: Memory host: save, forget and approve
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete host mutations while refusing modifications of repo-only project notes.

**Motivation** — This feature is the first surface: the agent sees an index of what earlier sessions saved, reads notes on demand, saves what a future session would need, and the user can inspect and edit memory from the terminal.

**Approach** — The save / forget / approve methods `host.ts` composes live in `host-writes.ts` (keeps `host.ts` under 400 lines).
- `save(write)` = `saveMemoryNote({ store, outbox, provider, logger, write, writeMode, source })`.
- `forget` and `approve` refuse a project slug that only a repo note holds with `NaxError` code `MEMORY_NOTE_READ_ONLY`, context `{ stage: "memory", slug }`, message `memory note "<slug>" is a repository note; edit .nax/memory/<slug>.md in the repository`; otherwise `forgetMemoryNote({ store, outbox, provider, logger, scope, slug, reason, writeMode })` and `approveMemoryNote({ store, scope, slug, logger })`.
`_memoryHostDeps = { memoryDirs, readRepoNotes, createMemoryStore, createMemoryOutbox, createLocalMemoryProvider, syncMemory, saveMemoryNote, forgetMemoryNote, approveMemoryNote }`.
Repo notes are never written by any tool or command.

**Scope** — In: host-writes.ts, replacement of the remaining host placeholders, direct/proposal pass-through, source propagation, repo-only refusal and original-file preservation. Out: tool error mapping (US-009), CLI write output (US-018/019), completing a proposal-mode forget and any nax-agent locking/validation changes. Saving a matching slug is allowed and creates a mirror shadow.

**Interface**
```ts
save(write: MemoryNoteWrite): Promise<MemorySaveResult>;
forget(input: { readonly scope: MemoryScope; readonly slug: string; readonly reason: string }): Promise<MemoryForgetResult>;
approve(input: { readonly scope: MemoryScope; readonly slug: string }): Promise<MemoryNote>;
```
Use feature-1 `MemorySaveResult { slug, status, delivered }`, `MemoryForgetResult { slug, status, delivered }`; validation/secret refusals are `MEMORY_WRITE_REFUSED`, absent forget/approve is `MEMORY_NOTE_NOT_FOUND`.

userStories.title: Memory tool provider: get and search
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the static nax-memory tool protocol and implement get/search.

**Motivation** — This feature is the first surface: the agent sees an index of what earlier sessions saved, reads notes on demand, saves what a future session would need, and the user can inspect and edit memory from the terminal.

**Approach** — Tool provider (`tool-provider.ts`)
`createMemoryToolProvider(host: MemoryHost): ToolProvider` returns `{ id: "nax-memory", kind: "static", stages: ["*"], instructions: async () => buildMemoryToolInstructions(), tools }` with four tools (precedent: `src/chat/background/tasks-provider.ts`). Every result is `{ content: <JSON> }` or `{ isError: true, content: "[memory] ..." }`; a tool never throws.

| Tool | Input (JSON schema, `additionalProperties: false`) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `get` | `slug` string (required), `scope` `"project" | "user"` | the note as JSON: `id, slug, type, scope, description, source, updatedAt, status, body` |
| `search` | `text` string (required), `scope`, `limit` integer 1-50 (default 10) | `{ "hits": MemoryHit[] }` |
| `save` | `slug`, `type`, `description`, `body` strings (required), `scope` | `{ slug, status, delivered }` |
| `forget` | `slug`, `reason` strings (required), `scope` | `{ slug, status, delivered }` |

`scope` defaults to `"project"`. `get` takes a slug only: design 6.6's `get { slug | id }` is narrowed, because ids are provider-internal and the index shows slugs. **Goal** — Register the memory CLI group and expose inspectable status and filtered lists.

**Motivation** — This feature is the first surface: the agent sees an index of what earlier sessions saved, reads notes on demand, saves what a future session would need, and the user can inspect and edit memory from the terminal.

**Approach** — CLI Behavior
`registerMemoryCommand(program, deps = _memoryCliDeps)` in `src/cli/memory.ts` adds the `memory` group; `bin/nax.ts` calls it beside `registerCostCommand(program)` and `src/cli/index.ts` exports it. Every subcommand takes `-d, --dir <path>` (default `process.cwd()`, the only `process.cwd()` read) and `--json`. Like `nax cost` it takes no trust gate and does not call `initLogger`: it writes only under `~/.nax/memory`. The repo root is resolved as `nax chat` resolves it: `naxDir = deps.findProjectDir(dir)`, `repoRoot = naxDir ? dirname(naxDir) : dir`, config `deps.loadConfig(naxDir ?? undefined)`. The host is created with `source: "human"` and a logger whose `warn` and `error` write `[memory] <message>` lines to stderr (`debug` and `info` are dropped), so a skipped repo note is visible at the terminal.

| Command | stdout (text) | `--json` stdout | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | `formatMemoryStatus(status)` (no index); `enabled: false` when disabled | `MemoryStatus`, or `{"enabled":false}` | 0 |
| `list [--type <t>] [--scope <s>]` | one `formatMemoryNoteLine` per note, project then user, each by slug | `{"notes":[...]}` (entries without `body`) | 0 |

Errors go to stderr as `Error: <message>` (also under `--json`) with exit 1: an unloadable config, a host creation failure, an invalid `--type` / `--scope`, a usage error (`--body` and `--body-file` both or neither given: `Error: give exactly one of --body or --body-file`), a refusal (an invalid `--type` on `save` surfaces as feature 1's refusal), an absent note (`Error: no memory note <scope>/<slug>`), a read-only note (its message), and every subcommand except `status` when memory is disabled (`Error: memory is disabled (memory.enabled is false)`).
`_memoryCliDeps = { findProjectDir, loadConfig, createMemoryHost, readFile, log, logErr, exit }`.

**Scope** — In: memory.ts registration/shared context, root/config resolution, CLI logger, status/list text+JSON and type/scope validation, barrel/bin registration. Out: show/sync (US-017), save (US-018), forget/approve (US-019); establish shared error/output conventions now for later handlers. No trust prompt or global logger initialization. Feature boundaries: `nax memory reset` is not built: with the `local` provider the mirror is the only copy of every note, so deleting it would destroy memory; it arrives with the remote provider. The koda remote provider, the `memory.koda` config block, `nax memory link` and provider-side search merging are the `memory-koda-provider` feature; `memory.provider` accepts only `local` here.

**Interface** — `registerMemoryCommand(program, deps = _memoryCliDeps)`, `_memoryCliDeps = { findProjectDir, loadConfig, createMemoryHost, readFile, log, logErr, exit }`. Use @/memory host/formatters and library-supported note types user/feedback/project/reference; list JSON strips body but retains source. Verification note: review bin registration and run `bun bin/nax.ts memory --help` from packages/nax outside automatic gates when appropriate.
